endorsements.quote: Operation requires continuous monitoring of performance, unintended use, information security threats, adverse events etc.
AI systems carry potential combined technical and clinical adversities, requiring aggregated reporting.

This includes upskilling and recruiting a more multidisciplinary workforce that in addition to healthcare professionals, possesses competence across data science, software engineering, software implementation and operation, data management, information security, law and policy, and quality assurance to perform these tasks.

unlisted_practices: Perform local validation of AI systems regardless of whether they are internally developed or procured.
Build an organizational support function with expertise in data selection and assessment, testing requirements, and verification metrics to support AI validation.
Build the management, competence, and infrastructure to use hospital health data to improve healthcare.
Establish software and data pipeline infrastructure that enables continuous integration and updating of AI systems.
Develop data governance and management beyond administrative use cases, with accessible standardized data formats and databases.
Develop a thorough understanding of the data used for AI development and avoid using administrative data such as ICD codes as ground truth labels for AI.
Adopt more agile, software-development-like management approaches in parts of the organization.

screen.reason: This is a discussion and gap-analysis paper applying the ISO 42001 standard to healthcare AI governance and hospital readiness.
